502	        self._last_num_atoms = num_atoms
503	        self._last_indices = getattr(g, "sample_idx", None)
504	
505	        return results, batch_size

507	    def training_step(self, batch: tuple, batch_idx: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
508	        """Training step that exposes per-sample preds and labels for callbacks.
509	
510	        Args:
511	            batch: Data batch.
512	            batch_idx: Batch index.
513	
514	        Returns:
515	            Dict with ``loss`` (used by Lightning for backprop) plus the raw ``preds``,
516	            ``labels`` tuples and per-sample ``indices`` / ``num_atoms`` so that callbacks
517	            such as :class:`matgl.utils.callbacks.PredictionLogger` can place predictions in
518	            a stable per-sample order across shuffled epochs.
519	        """
520	        loss = super().training_step(batch, batch_idx)
521	        return {
522	            "loss": loss,
523	            "preds": self._last_preds,
524	            "labels": self._last_labels,

538	            ``indices`` / ``num_atoms`` (the latter only present when the dataset has been
539	            stamped with :func:`matgl.utils.callbacks.add_sample_indices`).
540	        """

544	            "preds": self._last_preds,

550	    def loss_fn(
551	        self,
552	        loss: nn.Module,
553	        labels: tuple,
554	        preds: tuple,
555	        num_atoms: torch.Tensor | None = None,
556	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
557	        """Compute losses for EFS.
558	
559	        Args:
560	            loss: Loss function.
561	            labels: Labels.
562	            preds: Predictions
563	            num_atoms: Number of atoms.
564	
565	        Returns::
566	
567	            {
568	                "Total_Loss": total_loss,
569	                "Energy_MAE": e_mae,
570	                "Force_MAE": f_mae,
571	                "Stress_MAE": s_mae,
572	                "Magmom_MAE": m_mae,
573	                "Charge_MAE": q_mae,
574	                "Energy_RMSE": e_rmse,
575	                "Force_RMSE": f_rmse,
576	                "Stress_RMSE": s_rmse,
577	                "Magmom_RMSE": m_rmse,
578	                "Charge_RMSE": q_rmse
579	            }
580	
581	        """
582	        # labels and preds are (energy, force, stress, (optional) site_wise)
583	        if num_atoms is None:
584	            num_atoms = torch.ones_like(preds[0])
585	        if self.allow_missing_labels:
586	            valid_labels, valid_preds = [], []
587	            for index, label in enumerate(labels):
588	                valid_value_indices = ~torch.isnan(label)
589	                valid_labels.append(label[valid_value_indices])
590	                if index == 0:
591	                    valid_num_atoms = num_atoms[valid_value_indices]
592	                    pred = preds[index].view(1) if preds[index].shape == torch.Size([]) else preds[index]
593	                else:
594	                    pred = preds[index]
595	                valid_preds.append(pred[valid_value_indices])
596	        else:
597	            valid_labels, valid_preds = list(labels), list(preds)
598	            valid_num_atoms = num_atoms
599	
600	        # Per-atom energies are reused three times (loss, MAE, RMSE) — hoist
601	        # the divisions out of the metric calls so each tensor is materialised
602	        # once per loss_fn invocation.
603	        e_label_per_atom = valid_labels[0] / valid_num_atoms
604	        e_pred_per_atom = valid_preds[0] / valid_num_atoms
605	
606	        e_loss = self.loss(e_label_per_atom, e_pred_per_atom, **self.loss_params)
607	        f_loss = self.loss(valid_labels[1], valid_preds[1], **self.loss_params)
608	
609	        e_mae = self.mae(e_label_per_atom, e_pred_per_atom)
610	        f_mae = self.mae(valid_labels[1], valid_preds[1])
611	
612	        e_rmse = self.rmse(e_label_per_atom, e_pred_per_atom)
613	        f_rmse = self.rmse(valid_labels[1], valid_preds[1])
614	
615	        s_mae = torch.zeros(1)
616	        s_rmse = torch.zeros(1)
617	
618	        m_mae = torch.zeros(1)
619	        m_rmse = torch.zeros(1)
620	
621	        q_mae = torch.zeros(1)
622	        q_rmse = torch.zeros(1)
623	
624	        total_loss = self.energy_weight * e_loss + self.force_weight * f_loss
625	
626	        if self.model.calc_stresses:
627	            s_loss = loss(valid_labels[2], valid_preds[2], **self.loss_params)
628	            s_mae = self.mae(valid_labels[2], valid_preds[2])
629	            s_rmse = self.rmse(valid_labels[2], valid_preds[2])
630	            total_loss = total_loss + self.stress_weight * s_loss
631	
632	        if self.model.calc_magmom and labels[3].numel() > 0:
633	            if self.magmom_target == "symbreak":
634	                # Each metric was being recomputed twice for the +/- predictions; cache
635	                # the four tensors and pick the per-element minimum at the end.
636	                neg_pred = -valid_preds[3]
637	                m_loss = torch.min(
638	                    loss(valid_labels[3], valid_preds[3], **self.loss_params),
639	                    loss(valid_labels[3], neg_pred, **self.loss_params),
640	                )
641	                m_mae = torch.min(self.mae(valid_labels[3], valid_preds[3]), self.mae(valid_labels[3], neg_pred))
642	                m_rmse = torch.min(self.rmse(valid_labels[3], valid_preds[3]), self.rmse(valid_labels[3], neg_pred))
643	            else:
644	                labels_3 = torch.abs(valid_labels[3]) if self.magmom_target == "absolute" else valid_labels[3]
645	                m_loss = loss(labels_3, valid_preds[3], **self.loss_params)
646	                m_mae = self.mae(labels_3, valid_preds[3])
647	                m_rmse = self.rmse(labels_3, valid_preds[3])
648	            total_loss = total_loss + self.magmom_weight * m_loss
649	
650	        if self.model.calc_charge:
651	            q_loss = loss(labels[3], preds[3])
652	            q_mae = self.mae(labels[3], preds[3])
653	            q_rmse = self.rmse(labels[3], preds[3])
654	            total_loss = total_loss + self.charge_weight * q_loss
655	
656	        return {
657	            "Total_Loss": total_loss,
658	            "Energy_MAE": e_mae,
659	            "Force_MAE": f_mae,
660	            "Stress_MAE": s_mae,
661	            "Magmom_MAE": m_mae,
662	            "Charge_MAE": q_mae,
663	            "Energy_RMSE": e_rmse,
664	            "Force_RMSE": f_rmse,
665	            "Stress_RMSE": s_rmse,
666	            "Magmom_RMSE": m_rmse,
667	            "Charge_RMSE": q_rmse,
668	        }

671	def fit_element_refs(
672	    structures: Iterable[Structure],
673	    energies: ArrayLike,
674	    element_types: Sequence[str],
675	    *,
676	    rcond: float | None = None,
677	) -> np.ndarray:
678	    r"""Fit per-element energy offsets via linear regression.
679	
680	    Solves the least-squares problem
681	
682	    .. math::
683	
684	        E_i \approx \sum_{Z \in S} \mu_Z \, N_{i,Z}
685	
686	    where :math:`E_i` is the total energy of structure :math:`i`,
687	    :math:`N_{i,Z}` is the count of element :math:`Z` in that structure,
688	    and :math:`\mu_Z` is the per-element offset returned in the same
689	    order as ``element_types``. The result is shaped to drop straight
690	    into :class:`PotentialLightningModule` or
691	    :class:`matgl.apps.pes.Potential` as ``element_refs``.
692	
693	    Subtracting these offsets from the targets removes the (usually
694	    dominant) constant-per-element contribution from the loss so the
695	    model only has to learn the relative-energy surface. This stabilises
696	    training when the absolute energy scale (~tens of eV per atom) is
697	    large compared to the residual variation across a chemically
698	    homogeneous training set.
699	
700	    Args:
701	        structures: Iterable of pymatgen ``Structure`` (or ``Molecule``)
702	            objects. Composition is read via ``site.specie.symbol``.
703	        energies: Total potential energies, one per structure, in any
704	            unit consistent with downstream training (usually eV).
705	        element_types: Element ordering used by the model — typically
706	            the value of ``model.element_types`` or what
707	            ``matgl.ext.pymatgen.get_element_list`` returns. The output
708	            offset vector is in this order.
709	        rcond: Forwarded to ``numpy.linalg.lstsq``. ``None`` (default)
710	            uses NumPy's current default cutoff for small singular
711	            values; pass ``-1`` to retain old behaviour, or a float to
712	            override.
713	
714	    Returns:
715	        ``np.ndarray`` of shape ``(len(element_types),)`` with the fitted
716	        per-element offsets, dtype ``float64``.
717	
718	    Raises:
719	        ValueError: If ``structures`` and ``energies`` have different
720	            lengths, or if a structure contains an element not listed in
721	            ``element_types``.
722	
723	    Note:
724	        For inputs already in graph form (e.g. an
725	        :class:`~matgl.graph.data.MGLDataset` of PyG ``Data``
726	        objects), :meth:`matgl.layers.AtomRef.fit` provides the same
727	        regression directly on the layer.
728	
729	    Example:
730	        >>> from matgl.ext.pymatgen import get_element_list
731	        >>> elements = get_element_list(structures)
732	        >>> refs = fit_element_refs(structures, energies, elements)
733	        >>> module = PotentialLightningModule(model=model, element_refs=refs)
734	    """
735	    element_types = tuple(element_types)
736	    if not element_types:
737	        raise ValueError("element_types must be non-empty.")
738	
739	    z_to_col = {sym: i for i, sym in enumerate(element_types)}
740	    structures_list = list(structures)
741	    energies_arr = np.asarray(energies, dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1)
742	
743	    if len(structures_list) != energies_arr.shape[0]:
744	        raise ValueError(
745	            f"len(structures)={len(structures_list)} does not match len(energies)={energies_arr.shape[0]}."
746	        )
747	    if not structures_list:
748	        raise ValueError("structures must be non-empty.")
749	
750	    counts = np.zeros((len(structures_list), len(element_types)), dtype=np.float64)
751	    for i, struct in enumerate(structures_list):
752	        for site in struct:
753	            sym = site.specie.symbol
754	            col = z_to_col.get(sym)
755	            if col is None:
756	                raise ValueError(
757	                    f"Structure {i} contains element {sym!r} which is not in element_types={element_types}."
758	                )
759	            counts[i, col] += 1.0
760	
761	    refs, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(counts, energies_arr, rcond=rcond)
762	    return refs
763

765	def xavier_init(model: nn.Module, gain: float = 1.0, distribution: Literal["uniform", "normal"] = "uniform") -> None:
766	    """Xavier initialization scheme for the model.
767	
768	    Args:
769	        model (nn.Module): The model to be Xavier-initialized.
770	        gain (float): Gain factor. Defaults to 1.0.
771	        distribution (Literal["uniform", "normal"], optional): Distribution to use. Defaults to "uniform".
772	    """
773	    if distribution == "uniform":
774	        init_fn = nn.init.xavier_uniform_
775	    elif distribution == "normal":
776	        init_fn = nn.init.xavier_normal_
777	    else:
778	        raise ValueError(f"Invalid distribution: {distribution}")
779	
780	    for name, param in model.named_parameters():
781	        if name.endswith(".bias"):
782	            param.data.fill_(0)
783	        elif param.dim() < 2:  # torch.nn.xavier only supports >= 2 dim tensors
784	            bound = gain * math.sqrt(6) / math.sqrt(2 * param.shape[0])
785	            if distribution == "uniform":
786	                param.data.uniform_(-bound, bound)
787	            else:
788	                param.data.normal_(0, bound**2)
789	        else:
790	            init_fn(param.data, gain=gain)

799	# Stress-unit conversion to matgl's internal unit (**GPa**, compressive =
800	# negative — see the "Model Training" section of the README). ``1 GPa = 10
801	# kbar = 1/160.21766208 eV/Å³``. The ``"kbar"`` factor is ``-0.1``, which both
802	# rescales (kbar → GPa, /10) **and** flips the sign from VASP's
803	# compressive-positive convention to matgl's compressive-negative one — i.e.
804	# applying ``stress_unit="kbar"`` is exactly the README's "multiply VASP
805	# stresses by -0.1" recipe in one step. MatPES files ship raw VASP stress in
806	# kbar, hence the default; pass ``stress_unit="GPa"`` to skip the conversion
807	# or ``"eV/A3"`` if your file is already in eV/Å³ (magnitude only — supply the
808	# sign yourself for ``eV/A3``).
809	StressUnit = Literal["kbar", "GPa", "eV/A3"]
810	_STRESS_UNIT_TO_GPA: dict[str, float] = {
811	    "GPa": 1.0,
812	    "kbar": -0.1,
813	    "eV/A3": 160.21766208,
814	}

819	# Bader analysis ships in the top-level ``bader_charges`` field as electron
820	# counts (e); CM5 charges under the top-level ``cm5_partial_charges``. Any of
821	# the three can be ``None`` for a given sample if the upstream calculation
822	# failed.
823	ChargesSource = Literal["bader", "ddec6", "cm5"]
824	MagmomsSource = Literal["bader", "ddec6"]

863	    label: str,
864	    extractors: Mapping[str, tuple[str, Any]],
865	    default_source: str,
866	) -> tuple[str, Any] | None:

870	    ``False`` returns ``None`` (skip extraction).
871	    """

882	def _matpes_samples_to_lists(
883	    samples: Iterable[Mapping],
884	    stress_unit: StressUnit = "kbar",
885	    *,
886	    include_charges: bool | ChargesSource = False,
887	    include_magmoms: bool | MagmomsSource = False,
888	) -> tuple[list[Structure], dict[str, list]]:
889	    """Walk a MatPES sample list and return parallel structures + labels dict.
890	
891	    Always extracts ``energies``, ``forces``, and ``stresses``. Per-atom optional
892	    partial-charge / magmom fields are extracted when the corresponding
893	    ``include_*`` flag is truthy; samples whose requested optional field is
894	    ``None`` (i.e. the upstream calculation failed) are dropped from every
895	    parallel list, so the returned lists stay aligned.
896	
897	    Args:
898	        samples: Iterable of MatPES sample dicts.
899	        stress_unit: On-disk stress unit; see :meth:`MGLDatasetLoader.from_json`.
900	        include_charges: If truthy, extract per-atom partial charges under the
901	            label key ``"charges"`` and drop samples with missing values.
902	            ``True`` selects DDEC6 net atomic charges
903	            (``ddec6.partial_charges``, the matgl default for QET-style
904	            training); pass ``"bader"`` for Bader electron counts
905	            (``bader_charges``) or ``"cm5"`` for CM5 charges
906	            (``cm5_partial_charges``).
907	        include_magmoms: If truthy, extract per-atom magnetic moments under
908	            ``"magmoms"`` and drop samples with missing values. ``True``
909	            selects DDEC6 spin moments (``ddec6.spin_moments``); pass
910	            ``"bader"`` for Bader magmoms (``bader_magmoms``).
911	
912	    Returns:
913	        ``(structures, labels)`` where ``labels`` has keys ``"energies"``,
914	        ``"forces"``, ``"stresses"``, and optionally ``"charges"`` / ``"magmoms"``.
915	    """
916	    # (display_name, extractor_callable) tuples, one per enabled optional.
917	    enabled: list[tuple[str, str, Any]] = []
918	    charges_resolved = _resolve_optional_source(include_charges, "charges", _CHARGES_EXTRACTORS, "ddec6")
919	    if charges_resolved is not None:
920	        enabled.append(("charges", *charges_resolved))
921	    magmoms_resolved = _resolve_optional_source(include_magmoms, "magmoms", _MAGMOMS_EXTRACTORS, "ddec6")
922	    if magmoms_resolved is not None:
923	        enabled.append(("magmoms", *magmoms_resolved))
924	
925	    structures: list[Structure] = []
926	    energies: list[float] = []
927	    forces: list = []
928	    stresses: list = []
929	    optional_lists: dict[str, list] = {label: [] for label, _, _ in enabled}
930	    factor = _STRESS_UNIT_TO_GPA[stress_unit]
931	    dropped = 0
932	
933	    for raw in samples:
934	        # Skip samples missing any requested optional field. We check before
935	        # appending anything to keep the parallel lists in lockstep.
936	        skip = False
937	        optional_values: dict[str, list] = {}
938	        for label, _src_name, extractor in enabled:
939	            value = extractor(raw)
940	            if value is None:
941	                skip = True
942	                break
943	            optional_values[label] = np.asarray(value, dtype="float64").tolist()
944	        if skip:
945	            dropped += 1
946	            continue
947	
948	        struct = raw["structure"]
949	        if not isinstance(struct, Structure):
950	            struct = Structure.from_dict(struct)
951	        structures.append(struct)
952	        energies.append(float(raw["energy"]))
953	        forces.append(np.asarray(raw["forces"], dtype="float64").tolist())
954	        stresses.append((np.asarray(raw["stress"], dtype="float64") * factor).tolist())
955	        for label, val in optional_values.items():
956	            optional_lists[label].append(val)
957	
958	    labels: dict[str, list] = {"energies": energies, "forces": forces, "stresses": stresses, **optional_lists}
959	    if dropped and enabled:
960	        import warnings
961	
962	        missing = ", ".join(f"{label}({src})" for label, src, _ in enabled)
963	        warnings.warn(
964	            f"Dropped {dropped} MatPES samples missing one of: {missing}.",
965	            UserWarning,
966	            stacklevel=2,
967	        )
968	    return structures, labels

1010	def _build_pes_dataset(
1011	    structures: Sequence[Structure],
1012	    labels: Mapping[str, list],
1013	    *,
1014	    cutoff: float,
1015	    element_types: tuple[str, ...] | None,
1016	    save_cache: bool,
1017	    root: str | None,
1018	) -> MGLDataset:
1019	    """Construct an ``MGLDataset`` from parallel structure / label lists."""
1020	    # Lazy imports to avoid circulars (``matgl.utils.training`` is foundational).
1021	    from matgl.ext.pymatgen import Structure2Graph, get_element_list
1022	    from matgl.graph.data import MGLDataset
1023	
1024	    if element_types is None:
1025	        element_types = get_element_list(list(structures))

1201	          MSONable ``as_dict()`` form — anything ``Structure.from_dict`` can
1202	          rebuild. Carries the atomic positions, lattice, and species.

1309	            token=self.token,
1310	            cache_dir=self.cache_dir,
1311	        )

Now I understand the structure. The `MGLPotentialTrainer.fit` currently does not validate that the dataset's element_types match the model's element_types. The mismatch case uses model element_types ["Li", "O"] and dataset converter element_types ["O", "Li"]. During graph conversion, the atom types encoded by Structure2Graph will be according to the dataset's element_types order. Then the model's embedding layer is indexed by the model's element_types order, so the training silently trains with mismatched embeddings (atoms get mapped to wrong element embeddings).

We need to add a guard in `source/` that raises ValueError when the dataset's element_types and the model's element_types mismatch, before any fit/test work (fit_calls == 0, test_calls == 0).

The question is where should the guard live? Probably in `MGLPotentialTrainer.fit` — comparing `self.model.element_types` and `dataset.element_types`. Let's inspect MGLDataset and TensorNet models to see what attributes are available.

438	            )

440	            if self.clear_processed:

443	            self.graphs = graphs
444	            self.lattices = lattices
445	            self.state_attr = state_attrs_tensor

448	            if not self.graphs:

452	    def save(self) -> None:
453	        """Save PyG graphs, labels, and a cache fingerprint to processed_dir."""
454	        if not self.save_cache:

456	
457	        root = Path(self.root)

470	        fingerprint = _compute_cache_fingerprint(self.converter, self.include_line_graph, self.include_ref_charge)

473	    def load(self) -> None:

14	class GraphConverter(metaclass=abc.ABCMeta):
15	    """Abstract base class for converters from input crystals/molecules to graphs."""
16	
17	    @abc.abstractmethod
18	    def get_graph(self, structure) -> tuple[Data, torch.Tensor, list | np.ndarray]:
19	        """Get a graph from a structure.
20	
21	        Args:
22	            structure: Input crystal or molecule (e.g., Pymatgen structure or molecule).
23	
24	        Returns:
25	            Tuple containing:
26	            - Data: PyTorch Geometric Data object with edge_index, node features, and edge attributes.
27	            - torch.Tensor: Lattice matrix.
28	            - Union[List, np.ndarray]: State attributes.
29	        """
30	
31	    def get_graph_from_processed_structure(
32	        self,
33	        structure,
34	        src_id: list[int] | np.ndarray | torch.Tensor,
35	        dst_id: list[int] | np.ndarray | torch.Tensor,
36	        images: np.ndarray | torch.Tensor,
37	        lattice_matrix: np.ndarray | torch.Tensor,
38	        element_types: tuple[str, ...],
39	        frac_coords: np.ndarray | torch.Tensor,
40	        is_atoms: bool = False,
41	    ) -> tuple[Data, torch.Tensor, np.ndarray]:
42	        """Construct a PyTorch Geometric Data object from processed structure and bond information.
43	
44	        Args:
45	            structure: Input crystal or molecule (Pymatgen structure, molecule, or ASE atoms).
46	            src_id: Site indices for starting point of bonds.
47	            dst_id: Site indices for destination point of bonds.
48	            images: Periodic image offsets for the bonds.
49	            lattice_matrix: Lattice information of the structure.
50	            element_types: Element symbols of all atoms in the structure.
51	            frac_coords: Fractional coordinates of all atoms (or Cartesian for molecules).
52	            is_atoms: Whether the input structure is an ASE Atoms object.
53	
54	        Returns:
55	            Tuple containing:
56	            - Data: PyTorch Geometric Data object with edge_index, node features, and edge attributes.
57	            - torch.Tensor: Lattice matrix.
58	            - np.ndarray: State attributes.
59	        """
60	        # Create edge_index from src_id and dst_id
61	        src_id = torch.as_tensor(src_id, dtype=matgl.int_th)
62	        dst_id = torch.as_tensor(dst_id, dtype=matgl.int_th)
63	        edge_index = torch.stack([src_id, dst_id], dim=0)
64	
65	        device = edge_index.device
66	
67	        # Create Data object
68	        graph = Data(num_nodes=len(structure), edge_index=edge_index)
69	
70	        # Add periodic boundary condition (PBC) offset as edge attribute
71	        pbc_offset = torch.as_tensor(images, dtype=matgl.float_th, device=device)
72	        graph.pbc_offset = pbc_offset  # Store as edge_attr instead of separate pbc_offset
73	
74	        # Convert lattice matrix to tensor. Callers occasionally pass a list of
75	        # numpy arrays (e.g. ``[lattice_matrix]`` for a single periodic cell);
76	        # routing those through ``np.asarray`` first avoids the
77	        # "Creating a tensor from a list of numpy.ndarrays is extremely slow"
78	        # warning from ``torch.as_tensor``. We also force a copy when the array
79	        # is not writable (``pymatgen``'s ``Lattice.matrix`` returns a
80	        # read-only array, and ``np.expand_dims`` propagates that flag) since
81	        # PyTorch warns when constructing a tensor from a non-writable array.
82	        if not isinstance(lattice_matrix, torch.Tensor):
83	            lattice_matrix = np.asarray(lattice_matrix)
84	            if not lattice_matrix.flags.writeable:
85	                lattice_matrix = lattice_matrix.copy()
86	        lattice = torch.as_tensor(lattice_matrix, dtype=matgl.float_th, device=device)
87	
88	        # Create node features (node_type based on element indices). Use a dict
89	        # lookup instead of list.index() so the cost is O(N_atoms) rather than
90	        # O(N_atoms * len(element_types)) — meaningful on chemically diverse
91	        # datasets (alloys, MatPES) where element_types can be 80+ entries long.
92	        element_to_index = {elem: idx for idx, elem in enumerate(element_types)}
93	        if is_atoms:
94	            node_type = np.fromiter(
95	                (element_to_index[elem] for elem in structure.get_chemical_symbols()),
96	                dtype=np.int64,
97	                count=len(structure),
98	            )
99	        else:
100	            node_type = np.fromiter(
101	                (element_to_index[site.specie.symbol] for site in structure),
102	                dtype=np.int64,
103	                count=len(structure),
104	            )
105	        graph.node_type = torch.tensor(node_type, dtype=torch.long, device=device)  # Node features
106	
107	        # Add fractional coordinates as node attribute
108	        graph.frac_coords = torch.as_tensor(frac_coords, dtype=matgl.float_th, device=device)
109	
110	        # Default state attributes
111	        state_attr = np.array([0.0, 0.0], dtype=matgl.float_np)
112	
113	        return graph, lattice, state_attr

2	
3	``AtomRef`` adds a per-element constant offset to a model's prediction --
4	the standard isolated-atom (or "elemental reference") correction used when
5	training PES models on cohesive energies or absolute DFT energies.
6	"""
7	
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
11	
12	import numpy as np
13	import torch
14	from torch import nn
15	from torch_geometric.nn import global_add_pool
16	
17	if TYPE_CHECKING:
18	    from torch_geometric.data import Data
19	
20	
21	class AtomRef(nn.Module):
22	    """Get total property offset for a system."""
23	
24	    def __init__(self, property_offset: torch.Tensor | None = None, max_z: int = 89) -> None:
25	        """Initialize the AtomRef.
26	
27	        Args:
28	            property_offset (Tensor): a tensor containing the property offset for each element
29	                if given, max_z is ignored, and the size of the tensor is used instead
30	            max_z (int): maximum atomic number.
31	        """
32	        super().__init__()
33	        if property_offset is None:
34	            property_offset = torch.zeros(max_z, dtype=torch.float32)
35	        elif isinstance(property_offset, np.ndarray | list):  # for backward compatibility of saved models
36	            property_offset = torch.tensor(property_offset, dtype=torch.float32)
37	
38	        self.max_z = property_offset.shape[-1]
39	        self.register_buffer("property_offset", property_offset)
40	
41	    def get_feature_matrix(self, graphs: list[Data]) -> np.ndarray:
42	        """Get the number of atoms for different elements in the structure.
43	
44	        Args:
45	            graphs (list): a list of PyG Data objects
46	
47	        Returns:
48	            features (np.ndarray): a matrix (num_structures, num_elements)
49	        """
50	        features = torch.zeros(len(graphs), self.max_z, dtype=torch.float32)
51	        for i, graph in enumerate(graphs):
52	            node_types = graph.node_type  # Node types stored in graph.x
53	            features[i] = torch.bincount(node_types, minlength=self.max_z)
54	        return features.cpu().numpy()
55	
56	    def fit(self, graphs: list[Data], properties: torch.Tensor) -> None:
57	        """Fit the elemental reference values for the properties.
58	
59	        Args:
60	            graphs: PyG Data objects
61	            properties (torch.Tensor): tensor of extensive properties
62	        """
63	        features = self.get_feature_matrix(graphs)
64	        self.property_offset = torch.tensor(
65	            np.linalg.pinv(features.T @ features) @ features.T @ np.array(properties), dtype=torch.float32
66	        )
67	
68	    def forward(self, g: Data, state_attr: torch.Tensor | None = None):
69	        """Get the total property offset for a system.
70	
71	        Args:
72	            g: a batch of PyG graphs (torch_geometric.data.Data)
73	            state_attr: state attributes
74	
75	        Returns:
76	            offset_per_graph
77	        """
78	        # Gather per-atom offsets directly: shape (N,) or (S, N) for multi-state refs.
79	        # This replaces the previous (N, max_z) one-hot * repeat * multiply * sum pipeline,
80	        # which allocated max_z times the memory and FLOPs for the same result.
81	        batch = getattr(g, "batch", None)
82	        if self.property_offset.ndim > 1:
83	            # Multi-state: (S, max_z) -> per-atom (S, N) -> per-graph (S, B)
84	            atomic_offset = self.property_offset[:, g.node_type]  # (S, N)
85	            offset_per_graph = global_add_pool(atomic_offset.T, batch).T  # (S, B)
86	            return offset_per_graph[state_attr] if state_attr is not None else offset_per_graph
87	
88	        atomic_offset = self.property_offset[g.node_type]  # (N,)
89	        return global_add_pool(atomic_offset, batch)  # (B,)

def _validate_element_types(self, dataset: MGLDataset | Mapping[str, MGLDataset]) -> None:
        """Validate that the dataset's element ordering matches the wrapped model.

        Graph converters encode every node type as the index of its element in
        the converter's ``element_types`` sequence, while model embeddings are
        indexed by the model's own ``element_types`` sequence. The two orderings
        must therefore agree exactly; a same-set-different-order (or

                ``"train"`` / ``"valid"`` / ``"test"`` datasets.

            ValueError: If any dataset carries an element ordering different
                from ``self.model.element_types``.

        model_element_types = _element_types_of(self.model)
        if model_element_types is None:
            return

        for data in datasets:
            dataset_element_types = _element_types_of(data)
            if dataset_element_types is None:

            if dataset_element_types != model_element_types:

                    f"Dataset element types {dataset_element_types!r} do not match model element types "

def _element_types_of(obj: Any) -> tuple[str, ...] | None:
    """Return the element ordering carried by a model, dataset, or converter.

    if element_types is None:
